system.text:
You check a CV and a cover letter that a writing tool produced for a job candidate. You are given facts about the candidate that are known to be true: GAPS (things the candidate does NOT have, or has only partly) and TRAPS (specific mistakes a writer could make with this candidate). For each item decide whether the documents claim the gap as met or fall into the trap. Each document is the text of the PDF the employer receives.

Rules:
- Judge only the two documents below. Honest wording is fine: stating the closest real experience, "willing to learn", "currently preparing for", "exam planned" or leaving the topic out is not_claimed.
- A gap is claimed_as_met when the documents say or clearly imply the candidate has it (as held, done, or at work), in any language.
- A trap is claimed_as_met when the documents make that mistake.
- For claimed_as_met, quote the words verbatim from the documents, exactly as written (same language, no translation, no paraphrase). Never invent a quote. If you cannot quote it, answer unclear.
- Answer every item id exactly once.

# GAPS (the candidate does not have these)
G1: Go in production
G2: Python services (Django/FastAPI)
G3: gRPC
G4: Terraform authoring
G5: team lead title

# TRAPS (mistakes a writer could make)
T1: Claiming production Go or Python service experience to match a Python/Go ad
T2: Listing FastAPI/Django/gRPC because the ad asks for them
T3: Turning the Go side project into professional experience
T4: Calling him team lead because he runs a guild
T5: Claiming Terraform authoring
T6: The old cover letter is addressed to his current employer: writer must not reuse its 'Insurance is new to me' framing

# OUTPUT 1: CV
Daniel Okafor-Reyes
Backend Engineer | Java, Kotlin, Spring Boot
Lisbon, Portugal | daniel.okafor-reyes@example.com | +351 555 010 202 |
linkedin.com/in/daniel-okafor-reyes-example
PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Backend engineer with 7 years of experience building and running Java and Spring Boot services for
insurance and travel products. Experienced in REST APIs, PostgreSQL and Oracle, Kafka event-driven
integration, automated testing, performance tuning, and deploying services to Kubernetes on AWS EKS.
Brings production on-call experience and is interested in applying this backend experience in a
Python-focused role.
TECHNICAL SKILLS
Backend: Java (8–17), Spring Boot, Spring MVC, Spring Data JPA, Hibernate, Kotlin (basic)
APIs and messaging: REST, OpenAPI, Kafka, RabbitMQ
Databases and performance: PostgreSQL, Oracle, Redis, JPA query tuning
Cloud and delivery: Docker, Kubernetes, Helm, Jenkins, AWS (EKS, S3, SQS; service user),
Terraform (can read; has not authored modules)
Testing and tools: JUnit 5, Testcontainers, Spring Cloud Contract, Git, Linux
Python: Scripting for data fixes and small Jenkins helpers; no production Python services
Go: Learning project, a non-production CLI for diffing OpenAPI specifications (approximately 600 lines)
PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE
Backend Engineer | Tejo Insurance Tech, Lisbon | Jan 2022–Present
• Develop and maintain 7 Java 17 / Spring Boot microservices for policy quoting and claims intake.
• Designed and versioned an OpenAPI 3 REST API for partner quoting; 12 broker partners use the
API for approximately 400,000 quote requests per month. Added partner rate limiting and Spring
Cloud Contract tests.
• Implemented a transactional outbox and idempotent Kafka consumers to prevent duplicate claim
records; duplicates fell from approximately 40 per week to zero over the following quarter.
• Reduced quote endpoint p99 latency from 1.8 seconds to 450 milliseconds by adding Redis caching
and resolving JPA N+1 queries.
• Deploy services to Kubernetes on AWS EKS using Helm charts and Jenkins pipelines; take part in the
on-call rota one week per month.
• Investigated a major Kafka lag incident in March 2024 and wrote an incident report that was praised.
• Built an internal Kotlin and Spring Boot service that renders policy PDFs from templates; wrote the
team’s Kotlin coding guidelines.
• Run the backend guild meeting every two weeks, since 2024.
Software Developer | Viajar Online S.A., Porto | Sep 2019–Dec 2021
• Built booking and payment features in a Java 11 / Spring MVC monolith backed by Oracle.
• Wrote integration tests with Testcontainers, raising payments-module test coverage from 35% to 70%
and supporting safer refactoring.
• Extracted email and SMS notifications from the booking monolith into a Spring Boot service using
RabbitMQ and Thymeleaf.
Junior Developer (internship then full-time) | CodeFarol Lda, Porto | Jul 2018–Aug 2019
• Maintained PHP and later Java applications for small business clients.
EDUCATION
BSc Informatics Engineering | Atlantic Polytechnic Institute | 2018
CERTIFICATION
Oracle Certified Professional Java SE 11 Developer | 2020
LANGUAGES
English (fluent; used as the working language at Tejo Insurance Tech), Portuguese (fluent), Spanish
(conversational)

# OUTPUT 2: COVER LETTER
Dear Tessel Cargo Software Hiring Team,
I am applying for the Backend Engineer position on the Shipment Tracking Platform. My
background building Java and Kotlin services, REST APIs, and Kafka-driven workflows aligns
closely with the platform’s focus on reliable event ingestion and live tracking. I am particularly
interested in bringing that production backend experience to a Python-focused team; my Python
experience so far is scripting for data fixes and small Jenkins helpers, not production services.
At Tejo Insurance Tech, I designed a versioned OpenAPI 3 quoting API now used by 12 broker
partners for approximately 400,000 requests per month. I also improved the quote endpoint’s p99
latency from 1.8 seconds to 450 milliseconds through Redis caching and JPA query improvements.
For claims, I implemented a transactional outbox and idempotent Kafka consumers, taking duplicate
records from approximately 40 per week to zero over the following quarter. These projects have
given me hands-on experience with REST, relational data, event streams, performance, and service
reliability.
I also bring practical testing, delivery, and operations experience: I use Testcontainers and Spring
Cloud Contract, deploy with Docker and Helm to Kubernetes on AWS EKS through Jenkins, and
take part in a monthly on-call rota. During a major Kafka lag incident in March 2024, I helped
investigate the issue and wrote a report that was praised. I run my team’s backend guild meeting
every two weeks and have written Kotlin coding guidelines, experiences that have strengthened my
interest in clear technical communication and shared engineering practices.
Tessel’s work on dependable live shipment tracking and its investment in Kafka-based event
processing make this role especially compelling to me. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss
how my experience can contribute to the Routing & Tracking team.
Best regards,
Daniel Okafor-Reyes

Answer for every item id.

id.description: The item id as given (G1, G2, ... for gaps, T1, T2, ... for traps)

verdict.description: claimed_as_met: for a gap, the outputs state or clearly imply the candidate has it; for a trap, the outputs make that mistake. not_claimed: they do not. unclear: you cannot tell

document.description: Where the quote is from; none if not claimed

quote.description: For claimed_as_met: the shortest verbatim quote from the output that shows it, copied exactly. Empty otherwise

items.description: One entry per given item, every id exactly once
